subject: Network preflight + streaming SLO checklist for private inference
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Keller <alice.keller@acme-systems.com>, infra-eng@acme-systems.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Network preflight + streaming SLO checklist for private inference

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same expectations for a private/VPC proof-of-concept. I captured the performance items we discussed and what we need from ACME to validate them.

Summary of ACME requirements (as we understood on the call):
- Latency target: 15–25 ms p50, <= 60 ms p95 for inference requests from ACME app to Redwood private endpoint (end-to-end including network).
- Throughput: sustained 250 req/s, with ability to burst to ~1,000 req/s for short periods during peak traffic.
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent streaming sessions (long-poll/token streaming) with average message size ~300 tokens.
- Streaming: chunked token delivery with per-chunk flush target < 50 ms to preserve UI responsiveness.

What Redwood needs from ACME to validate these:
1) Network topology (VPN/peering details) and whether you prefer ExpressRoute/DirectConnect-style private peering or an IPsec VPN (we heard you have ExpressRoute).
2) Egress/NAT details and any outbound proxy or TLS inspection in the path. If there's a proxy that terminates TLS we need the hostname/IP and cert expectations.
3) MTU and any jumbo-frame configs on the path.
4) Scheduled test window (prefer a 2–3 day window) and a contact who can run iperf/traceroute/packet-capture on your side.
5) Acceptance SLOs you care most about (we proposed p50/p95 above — confirm).

Proposed Redwood deliverables for preflight:
- Perf harness (iperf + HTTP streaming runner) and instructions.
- A small set of ephemeral test endpoints + IP ranges (we'll provide).
- A scripted streaming test that exercises token streaming at target concurrency and reports per-chunk latency.

Attachments: call-recording-transcript.txt (short transcript), runbook-network-checklist.pdf (checklist we use for private deployments).

Next steps:
- ACME to confirm topology and proxy/NAT details by EOD Wed (2027-03-24).
- Redwood to share perf harness + IP ranges by Tue (2027-03-23).
- Schedule 2–3 day preflight test window (we proposed 2027-03-29 through 2027-03-31).

If the SLO targets above look off, call them out and we'll adjust; otherwise we'll kick off the perf plan early next week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Strategic Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0198

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network preflight + streaming SLO checklist for private inference

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. Couple clarifications from infra: we are on Azure with ExpressRoute private peering (no public egress for the private path). MTU is standard 1500; we do not use jumbo frames currently. Important callouts from our side:
- Outbound TLS inspection sits behind a proxy for certain subnets (we'll identify which ones); any IPs that will receive traffic must be allowed through the proxy and associated cert thumbprints validated.
- We will require that the Redwood private endpoint supports SNI-based routing (we have multiple hostnames behind our proxies).
- Availability target: we'd like to aim for 99.9% for the private path, but understand there may be differences vs hosted API; please confirm fallback behavior if private path is unavailable.

For the perf window: 2027-03-29 through 2027-03-31 works on our side but we need Redwood to provide the IP ranges and test harness by Tue 2027-03-23. We can run iperf and traceroute and share pcap if needed.

We attach a quick topology snapshot.

Cheers,
Alice Keller
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Systems

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network preflight + streaming SLO checklist for private inference

Forwarding ACME's notes — I drafted a concise test matrix and responsibilities table below so we can turn this into a runbook and share with ACME. Please review and flag anything missing.

Test matrix (proposed)
- Latency validation:
  - Redwood: run streaming test hitting private endpoint at 250 req/s sustained, measure p50/p95 per-chunk and end-to-end RTT.
  - ACME: run traceroute + tcpdump at app-facing subnet during test window.
- Throughput validation:
  - Redwood: ramp test from 50 -> 1,000 req/s across 4 slots (30 min each) to find sustainable throughput at target latency.
  - ACME: monitor CPU, NIC metrics and any egress throttling on their side.
- Concurrency validation:
  - Redwood: start 200 concurrent streaming sessions with average 300-token responses, assert per-session streaming flush < 50 ms.
  - ACME: ensure connection limits and load balancer configs allow 200+ concurrent connections.
- Fault/fallback validation:
  - Redwood: simulate endpoint unavailability and validate fallback to hosted API (if ACME permits failover).

Responsibilities
- Redwood (owner): perf harness, ephemeral endpoints + IP ranges, scripted streaming runner, data collection dashboard.
- ACME (owner): run iperf/traceroute, open firewall/proxy exceptions, capture tcpdump during tests, provide single infra contact.

I attached the perf-harness instructions I'll send to ACME (cleaned up for the runbook) — it includes how to run the streaming simulator and expected output schema.

If that looks good I'll publish as a short runbook and send to ACME with dates and the IP ranges.

-Lauren
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Keller <alice.keller@acme-systems.com>, infra-eng@acme-systems.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Network preflight + streaming SLO checklist for private inference

Appreciate the quick responses — finalizing the runbook and dates below. Confirmed items:
- Topology: ExpressRoute private peering (ACME) with MTU 1500 and outbound TLS inspection on select subnets (ACME to provide list).
- SLOs: target p50 20 ms, p95 <= 60 ms end-to-end; per-chunk streaming flush target < 50 ms. We set p50 20 ms to be slightly conservative vs earlier framing; we can adjust if ACME requests tighter numbers.
- Throughput/Concurrency: baseline 250 req/s sustained, burst tests to 1,000 req/s; 200 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Fallback: Redwood will verify hosted API fallback. Default behavior: if private endpoint is unreachable, we can fail open to hosted API provided ACME signs off on data handling for the fallback path. We will include a formal fallback run in the test matrix.

Action items and owners (short):
- ACME: provide list of subnets with TLS inspection + infra contact by EOD Wed 2027-03-24 (Alice).
- Redwood: share IP ranges + perf harness + ephemeral endpoints by Tue 2027-03-23 (Lauren). NOTE: Lauren is sending the harness today; IP ranges are attached in the runbook link.
- Joint: preflight test window 2027-03-29 through 2027-03-31. If that window doesn't work we'll move to 2027-04-05 through 2027-04-07.

Links and references:
- Runbook (draft): https://redwood.ai/drive/ACME-RWI-58-network-plan
- HubSpot deal: HS-987654

I'll send the formal runbook and a calendar invite for the kickoff. Thanks everyone — looking forward to the preflight.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Strategic Solutions, Redwood Inference
